title: Invariant logarithmic chart and stratum of a diagonal tame action
statement: Let $A$ be a strictly henselian Noetherian local ring, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $M$ be an fs log structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with sharp chart $a:Q\to M$ identifying $Q$ with the characteristic at the closed geometric point. Let a finite group $H$ of order $n$ invertible in $A$ act on this log scheme, trivially on its residue field. Suppose there is an $H$-fixed primitive $n$-th root of unity in $A$ and a character pairing $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes Q^{\rm gp}\to\mu_n(A)$ such that $h(a(q))=\chi_q(h)a(q)$. Put $I=(a(q):q\in Q\setminus\{0\})A$ and assume $H$ acts trivially on $A/I$. Put $B=A^H$, assume $A$ is finite over $B$, and set $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $f:X\to Y$. Define $L=\{q\in Q^{\rm gp}:\chi_q(h)=1\text{ for all }h\in H\}$ and $P=L\cap Q$. Then $P$ is fine saturated sharp, $P^{\rm gp}=L$, $L$ has finite index in $Q^{\rm gp}$ and contains $nQ^{\rm gp}$. The map $b:P\to B$, $p\mapsto a(p)$, is a chart of the invariant log sheaf $(f_*M)^H$ near the closed point and identifies $P$ with its characteristic there. With $J=(b(p):p\in P\setminus\{0\})B$, the natural map $B/J\to A/I$ is an isomorphism. For such data obtained by strict localization of a finite quotient of locally Noetherian fs log schemes, the chart is induced on a pointed etale neighbourhood of the quotient point. No regularity of $A/I$ or logarithmic dimension equality is assumed.

source.place: Exposé VI, Proposition 3.5(b), proof 3.7(b) and the stratum identification at the beginning of 3.7(c), printed pp.74–76; character convention 3.4.

proof.text: The affine $H$-scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is admissible, and the order of every geometric stabilizer divides the invertible integer $n$. Apply [lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient]: its affine quotient is precisely $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A^H)=Y$, a finite surjective quotient with orbit fibres and invariant structure sheaf, and $Y$ is Noetherian. The closed geometric point has stabilizer $H$, since $H$ fixes the residue field. As $A$ is strictly henselian, [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants] identifies the strict local ring of $Y$ at its image with $A^H=B$, compatibly with the original map from $B$. Thus $B$ is strictly henselian; it also identifies the invariant log stalk with $M_{\bar x}^H$ and its unit subgroup with $B^\times$. These are the actual invariant direct-image stalks.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), opening strict-local reduction; VI paragraph following 3.5 for the invariant direct image

proof.text: Use the specified chart $a$ and the specified pairing $\chi$ throughout. No replacement of this chart on a source neighbourhood is needed: the hypotheses already give $h(a(q))=\chi_q(h)a(q)$ and fixed roots of unity. Write $\alpha(a(q))$ simply as $a(q)$ when it is regarded as an element of $A$. At the closed point the sharp chart gives $M_{\bar x}=Q\oplus A^\times$, so the ideal generated by its nonunit log sections is exactly the stated $I$.

source.place: VI 3.4 and 3.7(b), the given diagonal chart

proof.text: Let $\varphi:Q^{\rm gp}\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_{\rm ab},\mu_n(A))$ be $q\mapsto(h\mapsto\chi_q(h))$. Its target is finite, so $L=\ker\varphi$ has finite index. Since every value has order dividing $n$, $nQ^{\rm gp}\subseteq L$. Put $P=L\cap Q$. If $p\in P^{\rm gp}$ and $rp\in P$ for some $r>0$, then $p\in Q^{\rm gp}$ and saturation of $Q$ gives $p\in Q$; also $P^{\rm gp}\subseteq L$ gives $p\in L$; hence $P$ is saturated, and it is sharp because it is a submonoid of sharp $Q$. To see finite generation, choose additive generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$. Every element of $P$ is congruent modulo $nQ$ to a sum $\sum_i e_iq_i$ with $0\le e_i<n$; because both the element and its $nQ$ part lie in $L$, retain only those finitely many residues that lie in $L$, together with $nq_1,\ldots,nq_s$. These generate $P$. Finally, if $\ell\in L$, write $\ell=u-v$ with $u,v\in Q$; then $n v\in P$ and $\ell+n v=u+(n-1)v\in P$, so $\ell\in P^{\rm gp}$. The reverse inclusion is immediate, hence $P^{\rm gp}=L.

source.place: Expose VI, proof 3.7(b), printed p.75, definition of $P' and $P=P'\cap Q$

proof.text: For the closed invariant stalk, write an invariant log section uniquely as $u\,a(q)$, with $u\in A^\times$, $q\in Q$. Its invariance says $h(u)\chi_q(h)=u$. Reduce this identity to the residue field: $H$ acts trivially there and $\bar u\ne0$, hence $\overline{\chi_q(h)}=1$. Reduction on $\mu_n(A)$ is injective: if $\zeta^n=1$ and $\zeta\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m_A}$, the factor $1+\zeta+\cdots+\zeta^{n-1}$ is a unit (its residue is $n$), so $(\zeta-1)(1+\cdots+\zeta^{n-1})=0$ forces $\zeta=1$. Consequently $q\in P$, and the original identity now gives $h(u)=u$. Conversely every $u\in B^\times$ and $p\in P$ gives an invariant section. Thus $M_{\bar x}^H=P\oplus B^\times$; fixed units are exactly $B^\times$ because their inverses are fixed. By the invariant-stalk identification, $P$ is the characteristic of $(f_*M)^H$ at the closed point. This argument explicitly includes the possible unit twist; it is not an argument about monomials alone.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), invariant chart in diagram (3.b); unit-twist verification at the closed point

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-tame-diagonal-standard-closed-immersion] to this finite quotient. Step 1 supplies its Noetherian quotient, orbit fibres and strict local rings, and the module-finiteness is assumed. The given diagonal chart has sharp characteristic $Q$, so $H$ fixes that characteristic; $n$ is invertible and the roots are fixed. Finally its trivial-stratum hypothesis is exactly the assumption that $H$ acts trivially on $A/I$. The cited statement gives the surjective $H$-equivariant ring homomorphism
$$C=B\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\longrightarrow A,\qquad b\otimes z^q\longmapsto b\,a(q).$$
In particular every element of $A$ is a finite sum $\sum_q b_q a(q)$ with $b_q\in B$. This is the strict closed immersion (3.c), whose proof in ILO uses triviality on the stratum, averaging and Nakayama; we use its stated surjectivity, not just the construction of the comparison morphism.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), map (3.c) and the averaging–Nakayama argument, printed p.76

proof.text: The same comparison node states more than surjectivity of a strict-local ring map: etale locally at both points, the charts $a,b$ of $X$ and of the actual invariant log structure $N=(f_*M)^H$ are represented on pointed source and target neighbourhoods $X',Y'$, with $X'\to Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ a strict closed immersion. Use its target-chart assertion. It identifies the log structure associated to $b:P\to B$ with $N$ on the quotient neighbourhood, hence on every geometric stalk there, not merely the closed stalk calculated in Step 4. The chart is by the fs monoid of Step 3 and its closed characteristic is the one from Step 4. For data obtained from a finite quotient before strict localization, the pointed etale neighbourhood $Y'$ in this cited assertion is precisely the required neighbourhood of the original quotient point. This uses an explicit theorem supplying target neighbourhoods and invariant charts; it does not descend the source neighbourhood from the equivariant-chart lemma by an unsupported claim that its quotient is etale.

source.place: VI Proposition 3.5(b), printed p.74, and proof 3.7(b), diagrams (3.b)–(3.c), printed pp.75–76

proof.text: For $p\in P$ the log section $a(p)$ is fixed, so its structural image lies in $B$ and is the asserted $b(p)$. The Reynolds operator $R(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h(x)$ maps $A$ to $B$. Since the action on $A/I$ is trivial, $R(x)\equiv x\pmod I$. Thus $B\to A/I$ is surjective. Since $J\subseteq B\cap I$, it induces a surjective map $B/J\to A/I$.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), surjectivity onto the stratum, printed p.76

proof.text:
To compute the kernel, use the $B$-monomial presentation of Step 5. An element $x\in I$ has an expression $\sum_q c_q a(q)$ with $q
e0$ and $c_q\in A$. Expand each $c_q$ as $\sum_r b_{q,r}a(r)$, $b_{q,r}\in B$. Then $x$ is a finite $B$-linear combination of monomials $a(q+r)$ with $q+r
e0$: if $q+r=0$ in sharp $Q$, both summands would be units, contrary to $q
e0$. For $t\in Q$, averaging a monomial gives $R(a(t))=a(t)$ when $t\in P$, and gives zero otherwise. Indeed, for a nontrivial $\chi_t$, choose $h_0$ with $\chi_t(h_0)
e1$. The sum $S=\sum_h\chi_t(h)$ satisfies $(\chi_t(h_0)-1)S=0$; the factor is a unit in $B$, by the injectivity of reduction on roots of unity proved in Step 4 and invariance of its inverse. Therefore $S=0$. If now $x\in B\cap I$, then $x=R(x)$ is a $B$-linear combination of the $a(p)$ with $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$, hence belongs to $J$. This proves $B\cap I=J$ and $B/J\simeq A/I$. The coefficients are invariant here because of the surjective comparison of Step 5; arbitrary coefficients in $A$ could have nontrivial characters and cannot be discarded by averaging.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), surjective comparison (3.c), and beginning of 3.7(c), stratum identification; expanded Reynolds calculation

All three points of the b716df3f RETURN are repaired. (1) Step 4 now handles the unit twist: h(u)χ_q(h)=u reduces to χ̄=1, and reduction is injective on μ_n because 1+…+ζ^{n-1}≡n is a unit; no cancellation of monomials is used. (2) Steps 5–6 cite the landed lem-per-tame-diagonal-standard-closed-immersion. Its statement makes a,b charts of X and of N=(q_*M)^G on pointed étale neighbourhoods and gives the surjection B⊗_{Z[P]}Z[Q]→A. All its hypotheses are supplied by Step 1 and the item's hypotheses (strictly local, so the stabilizer is H; the sharp chart gives an H-fixed characteristic). Y is strictly local, so the étale chart descends to Y, and the neighbourhood clause applies the node to the original quotient. (3) Step 8 expands each coefficient into B-monomials using that surjection before averaging, so the false claim about A-coefficients is gone; B∩I=J follows. Step 3 is checked: saturation starts in P^gp, finite generation uses residues mod nQ, and P^gp=L via ℓ+nv. Step 7 is the Reynolds surjection. Tested: Q=0; Q=N with the sign action; Q=N² with the diagonal sign, where P=⟨(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)⟩ and the off-origin characteristic is N both from the stalk and from the chart. No cycle: the 108-node closure of the cited nodes excludes the item and has no lem/thm-trf nodes. proof_deps equals the union of step uses, every step is under 2000 characters, and no SGA source is cited.
